context.checkin: I'm a teacher; I like a written plan. I worry about my heart and the twins.

facts.value: Cesarean section (secondary to vasa previa with twin gestation)
Maternal aunt with autoimmune thyroid disease
outpatient visit, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Dr. Elena Rodriguez
Persistent vaginal bleeding 4 weeks after spontaneous vaginal delivery
She reports persistent vaginal bleeding since delivery, which she describes as initially heavy and red, but now lighter and brownish. She denies any fever, abdominal pain, or foul-smelling discharge.
outpatient visit, Cardiology, Dr. Michael Chen
Gradually worsening shortness of breath since final weeks of pregnancy

The patient presents to the cardiology clinic six weeks after delivering a healthy baby via spontaneous vaginal delivery at term, returning for evaluation after her obstetrics visit four weeks prior for postpartum bleeding. She has a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy, impaired glucose tolerance, and postpartum thyroiditis, and reports gradually worsening shortness of breath which started during the final weeks of her pregnancy and has continued to worsen since childbirth.
ed visit, Emergency Medicine, Dr. Fatima Al-Hassan
Progressive shortness of breath, orthopnea, and bilateral leg swelling

The patient presents to the emergency department with worsening symptoms in the context of her known peripartum cardiomyopathy, previously evaluated by cardiology two months prior. She presents with a 2-week history of progressive shortness of breath, orthopnea, and bilateral leg swelling.
outpatient visit, Endocrinology, Dr. Robert Taylor
Palpitations, irritability, and 10-pound weight loss despite increased appetite
Patient with peripartum cardiomyopathy, seen in April, presents to the clinic 5 months postpartum. She denies any pain or discomfort in her neck.
outpatient visit, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Dr. Elena Rodriguez
Routine prenatal visit at 18 weeks of gestation with twin pregnancy

The patient is a 32-year-old female with a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy and postpartum thyroiditis following her delivery earlier this year who returns to the obstetrics clinic for routine prenatal care at 18 weeks gestation with a twin pregnancy. She presents to the obstetrics clinic.
ed visit, Emergency Medicine, Dr. James Wilson
Sudden onset of painless vaginal bleeding after feeling a pop in her abdomen

The patient, with a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy and postpartum thyroiditis after her first pregnancy and current twin gestation, presents with sudden onset of painless vaginal bleeding. She denies any trauma.
outpatient visit, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Dr. Elena Rodriguez
Postpartum check-up 8 weeks after delivering second child with increased thirst and frequent urination

Patient with history of peripartum cardiomyopathy and gestational diabetes returns for postpartum follow-up, reporting feeling generally well but mentions increased thirst and frequent urination. She notes uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery and currently breastfeeds.
outpatient visit, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Dr. Priya Natarajan
Request for elective cesarean delivery due to significant anxiety about labor and vaginal delivery

The patient is a 34-year-old female with a history of peripartum cardiomyopathy following her first delivery and vasa previa in her prior twin gestation who presents requesting elective cesarean delivery for her current pregnancy. She carries diagnoses of generalized anxiety disorder, impaired glucose tolerance, and prior postpartum thyroiditis.
You are uncomfortable performing a cesarean delivery without a clear medical or obstetric indication.
Cardiology: Heart follow-up with echo after pregnancy (in 2 days)

scenes.title: Welcome, Emily!
scenes.voiceover: Hi Emily, your heart follow-up visit is coming up soon.

scenes.title: What to Expect
scenes.text: We will check your heart with an echo.
scenes.voiceover: We will check your heart with an echo and talk about your care plan together.

scenes.title: How Long and Who Will Be There
scenes.voiceover: The visit will take about 40 minutes. Our cardiology team will be with you.

scenes.title: Your Choices
scenes.text: You can ask for a written plan.
scenes.voiceover: You can ask for a written summary or choose how you want to follow up.

scenes.title: Need Help?
scenes.voiceover: Call 555-0100 if you need help. We are here to support you.

scenes.title: Thank You, Emily!
scenes.voiceover: Thank you, Emily, for coming to your heart follow-up.

scenes.title: What We Did
scenes.text: We checked your heart and reviewed your plan.
scenes.voiceover: We checked your heart and reviewed your care plan together.

scenes.title: Next Steps
scenes.text: Follow your written plan and take your medicines.

scenes.title: When to Call
